An athlete is a person who participates in sports, physical games, or bodily exercises — especially one who does so with skill, training, and serious dedication. The word almost always suggests that the person has gone beyond just casual or occasional physical activity. An athlete trains, practises, and pushes their body toward a goal, whether that is winning a competition, breaking a record, or simply performing at a high level.

Think of a runner who wakes up every morning to train, or a swimmer who spends hours in the pool perfecting their technique. These people are athletes. The word carries a sense of commitment and physical ability that goes beyond what an ordinary person does for fun.

The word "athlete" is used in two slightly different ways depending on where you are in the world.

The broad sense (most common, especially in American English): An athlete is anyone who regularly plays a sport or engages in competitive physical activity — football players, basketball players, tennis players, gymnasts, boxers, cyclists, and so on. In this sense, the word covers almost every kind of sport imaginable.

The narrower sense (more common in British English): Here, "athlete" refers more specifically to someone who competes in track and field events — meaning running races, jumping events (like the long jump or high jump), and throwing events (like the shot put or javelin). When the British say "a world-class athlete," they often mean a runner or a field competitor, not a footballer or a cricketer.

In modern global usage, the broad sense is far more widespread and is what most people mean when they use the word.

Not every person who exercises or plays a game is typically called an athlete. The word implies a few important qualities:

Physical skill. An athlete has developed specific abilities — speed, strength, flexibility, coordination, endurance, or a combination of these — to a level that goes beyond the average person.

Training and discipline. Athletes don't just play casually. They follow structured training routines, watch their diet, rest carefully, and work on improving their performance consistently over time.

Competition or performance. Most athletes measure themselves against others or against a standard. They compete in matches, tournaments, races, or games. Even when training alone, the goal is usually to perform better in a competitive setting.

Dedication. Being an athlete is treated almost like a job or a serious commitment — not just a hobby. It demands time, sacrifice, and mental toughness alongside physical ability.

That said, the word is sometimes used loosely in everyday speech. Someone might say, "She's a natural athlete," simply meaning the person is physically gifted and picks up sports easily — even if they don't compete professionally.

Athletes come in many forms, and the word can be combined with other words to describe them more precisely.

A professional athlete is someone who is paid to compete in a sport. This is their career and main source of income. Think of footballers, NBA basketball players, or professional tennis players.

An amateur athlete participates in sports without being paid — purely out of love for the game or the challenge. Many Olympic athletes throughout history competed as amateurs.

A student athlete is someone (typically at a school or university) who both studies and competes in organised sports for their institution.

An Olympic athlete (or Olympian) is someone who has qualified to compete at the Olympic Games — one of the most prestigious titles an athlete can hold.

An elite athlete refers to someone at the very top of their sport — among the best in the world or in their country.

A complete athlete describes someone who excels across multiple physical dimensions — strength, speed, agility, endurance — rather than just one. It is a term of high praise.

Athlete vs. player vs. sportsperson: These words overlap, but "athlete" carries the strongest emphasis on physical conditioning, training, and bodily excellence. A "player" might simply refer to someone who plays a game. A "sportsperson" is a broader, more neutral term. "Athlete" is the most prestigious and disciplined-sounding of the three.

The body of an athlete: In everyday speech, people sometimes use the phrase "he/she has the body of an athlete" — meaning the person has a lean, strong, well-conditioned physique, even if they may not actively compete in sports.

Can non-traditional sports have athletes? Yes. In modern usage, people increasingly refer to chess players, esports competitors, or even dancers as athletes — or debate whether they should be called that. Strictly speaking, "athlete" refers to physical sporting activity, so these uses are informal or debated.

Since you are a learner, knowing the family of words connected to "athlete" will help you greatly.

Athletic (adjective) — This describes anything related to athletes or sport ("an athletic competition"), or it describes a person who has a strong, fit, well-built body ("She has an athletic figure"). It can also mean physically capable and agile.

Athletics (noun) — In the broad sense, this means sports and physical activities in general ("a career in athletics"). In the specific British/international sense, it refers to track and field events as a sport category.

Athleticism (noun) — This is the quality of being athletic — the combination of physical skill, strength, agility, and coordination that makes someone stand out as a natural mover. "His athleticism was on full display during the match."
How It Is Used in Sentences

Here are examples that show the word working naturally in different contexts:

  • "She became a professional athlete at the age of nineteen and went on to win three Olympic gold medals."
  • "The school provides scholarships to student athletes who excel both academically and in sport."
  • "He may not look like much, but he's a complete athlete — fast, strong, and incredibly agile."
  • "Even after retiring from competition, she stayed fit and kept the body of a true athlete."
  • "The country sent over 200 athletes to compete at the international games."
  • "Being an elite athlete requires years of sacrifice, discipline, and mental resilience."

Athlete is a word of respect. It recognises that a person has gone beyond casual physical activity and has devoted real effort to developing their body and skills for sport or competition. Whether they are a sprinter on a world stage or a dedicated amateur runner in their local club, the word honours their commitment to physical excellence.
